items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Letter signed 'your friend Bill Lambert' referencing playing together in Chicago at Lambs Cafe and Hoboken in 1915; Interviewee refers to him as 'that is a drummer of Brown's band'

ctx.x: From this article, many other articles was copied. This is a work, you've got to be either pro-communist or a communist to work this way. There's a letter to keep me quiet. I'm a working man, trying to support a family. This man has not stopped writing about Negroes, yet he knows different. Now here's Brown's letter. To show you Brown was lying, I want to show you, I want to have him read this in there, what the name of his band was, in case you ever read Downbeat on 1936, and see what they have did to a man who…

This is dated New Orleans, Louisiana, 10-21-36. Dear friend Nick, received your letter and was very glad to hear from you. Was glad to hear that you are in good health. as this letter leaves me the same. Was also glad to hear that you are doing good and hope you will continue to do so. If I remember correctly, the building of the band when we were in Chicago playing at the Lambs Cafe was Brown's Band from Dixieland. We opened an engagement there on a short time after May the 15th. Sorry I'm not able to furnish…

destroyed by fire since returning home we were built at a theater in Hoboken New Jersey as Brown's band Kings of Ragtime that was during the latter part of 1915 I think also played an engagement at the Century Theater in New York and played Lowe's it says Lowe's time as the musical rules give my regards to Larry Tony and any of the other boys I know my wife sends her best regards wishing you the best of luck and success I remain your friend Bill Lambert
